messages:
Maya (marketing): Quick ask — we need final messaging and a tiny rebut pack for Tuesday's webinar vs cloud AI platforms / LLM APIs / infra vendors. Can we iterate here?
Owen (sales): I can jump in. Biggest field objections we should pre-empt?
Li (product): Top three: vendor lock-in, opaque unit economics, and unpredictable tail latency under load. Keep counters short.
Samir (eng): FWIW our perf bench shows ~2x lower cost-per-token at similar p50 with batching + KV prefix cache vs managed endpoints. Want to be careful not to overclaim p99 improvements without region data.
Axel (growth): Draft A/B social headlines (short):
  A) "Predictable inference at half the cost"
  B) "Same latency, lower unit cost — prioritize serving economics, not model ownership"
Maya (marketing): I like B. Tweak to: "Same latency, lower unit cost — choose serving economics, not model ownership."
Owen (sales): Field rebut snippets (1-2 lines):
  - Objection: "We're on CloudX endpoints already."
  - Reply: "Cloud APIs are great for dev; in production teams run into opaque tail latency and runaway unit costs. Redwood adds routing, caching and fallbacks so you hit SLOs and predictable economics."
Li (product): Add micro-technical explanation for SREs (2 lines):
  "Runtime continuously batches requests, keeps per-session KV caches for prefix reuse, and auto-selects quantized kernels — reduces tokens and avoids repeated compute for common prefixes."
Samir (eng): Sample routing policy snippet we can show in a slide (one-code-block):
```json
{
  "route": "latency-first",
  "fallbacks": ["gpt-lite", "gpt-quant"],
  "cache_prefix": true,
  "batching": {"target_ms": 8}
}
```
Axel (growth): Inbound routing rules (short mapping):
  - keywords -> enterprise AE: "SLA", "on-prem", "data residency", "dedicated"
  - keywords -> SDR: "trial", "api key", "free credits", "embed"
  - score >= 75 -> Sales outreach, 40-74 -> SDR nurture, <40 -> marketing drip
  Regex examples: `/\b(SLA|latency|on-?prem(ise|ise)?|data residency|dedicated)\b/i`
Maya (marketing): Can someone draft a 1-paragraph benchmark narrative for the slide deck? Need plain language + one demo bullet.
Li (product): Draft paragraph: "In controlled dialog workloads, Redwood's serving runtime reduced cost-per-token by 1.8–2.4x vs major cloud managed endpoints while preserving comparable median latency. That improvement comes from continuous batching, prefix KV caching, and model-variant fallbacks — which we will demo with a live routing scenario showing an automatic fallback to a quantized variant under contention."
Owen (sales): Short demo CTA one-liner for slide: "See a live routing demo — register to reserve a dedicated capacity slot."
Axel (growth): Three quick sales soundbites (for call prep):
  1) "We help you avoid surprise inference bills while keeping latency predictable."
  2) "You can keep using the same models — we just serve them smarter."
  3) "Fallbacks + caching = fewer tokens billed, same user experience."
Maya (marketing): Perfect. I'll assemble a 1-pager and short deck callouts. @ops-bot can you create a doc + deck link under marketing assets? :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Created doc — https://internal.redwood/marketing/msg-lab-arena (permissions: marketing-read, engineering-read) :robot_face:
Owen (sales): I'll add objection training bullets to the one-pager after Maya drops the draft.
Samir (eng): I'll sanity-check the benchmark language and ping if we need to soften numbers.
Maya (marketing): Thanks team — aiming to freeze copy EOD tomorrow so design can finish slides. If anyone has alternate phrasing, drop it here.
